editorial: When Daadi Ki Shaadi turns a grandmother’s accidental social media post into a wedding calamity, you’re instantly swept into a whimsical family comedy that feels like a living romcom in a bustling urban setting. The film sets itself apart by layering generational perspectives, letting the elderly cast wield smartphones as new-age curses. The standout moment is when the grandma, played with fierce warmth, lets a playful smirk cut through the tension like a comic cue, turning potential disaster into a laugh-out-loud rally. Ideal for anyone who enjoys lighthearted, family-friendly movies that crack jokes while still nurturing heartfelt stakes. Only brief pacing hiccups appear toward the finale, but the script’s quick wit more than compensates for the slight slowdown.
